# The recorded class of each real-binary probe (tests/test_scope_probe_client.py).

# PASS names an observed class, not a blanket capability or provider guarantee.
# A diagnostic probe whose new run differs reports 'changed recorded=<class>';
# the correctness-essential classes are asserted by the probes themselves.
client probe CE: PASS class=CE-A
client probe DAH: PASS class=DAH-override
client probe U1: PASS class=U1-proc

client probe SF: PASS class=SF-lead-heavy
client probe RL: PASS class=RL-none
client probe RET: PASS class=RET-ok
client probe R19: PASS class=R19-closed
# R19: the compiled PreModelSwitch hook carries onFailure "block": a missing,
# non-executable, crashing or timed-out shim keeps the lead (without it the
# first three switch); deny and allow answers are unchanged. A shim exiting 0
# with a non-JSON answer gives no decision and the switch proceeds (the real
# shim answers its own deny on every failure).

# Supervisor takeover and staged marketplace-plugin updates remain INCONCLUSIVE

# The receipts below: signed client 2.1.310 linux-x64 (binary sha256
# b73676430af12f97316a798b8371f81d640f90a58bdcb8f3ce56a835bb47df56, release
# manifest sha256 895e85ce24c3df3fdb77ac1006bdb2b66f1c42dd557000e65ced1e4aad847e74),
# 2026-10-24.
#
# The session window's representation (tests/test_compaction_window_probe.py),
# session window 800000 at 90 %:
compaction window probe: PASS class=env-window-holds
# The compiled window variable: the lead compacts at 702000 fresh, on
# --resume, against user, project and local top-level, per-model and env
# values of 300000 and a process env of 300000, after /autocompact 300000
# (which saves nothing under the variable) and with a native --autocompact
# 1000000 (a launch refuses the flag; the variable outranks it anyway); a
# 128000-bound agent shares its 200K class's window (162000). A lead set bound
# at 80000 compacts at the client's 100K floor (67000; charmer compiles and
# shows 47000), never at the model's own default.
# Per-agent windows are not compiled: under the variable a 128000 agent
# window is ignored (162000). Recorded, never gating: a top-level
# autoCompactWindow with the variable "0" in the flag-settings env lowers an
# agent to its own window (95000 for 128000, 252000 for 300000 on a 1M agent;
# one above the class or below 100K is ignored) and holds the lead against the
# same user layers, /autocompact, --resume and --agent, but a native
# --autocompact 1000000 replaces it (no compaction by 800000) and an 80000
# lead set falls back to the model's own window (no compaction by 180000). Its
# survival of a supervisor takeover, a same-process /autocompact and a
# workflow agent's window are not measured offline, so it is not compiled.
# --autocompact as the representation passes the lead, user-layer and agent
# cases; /autocompact in a running session replaces it (read from the build).
#
# The auto-mode classifier's model (tests/test_auto_mode_model_probe.py):
client check auto-mode-model: PASS class=AM-owned
# Under --permission-mode auto offline the classifier never answers; the
# client's refusal names the model it chose. A CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL in
# the user, project or local settings env, fresh and on --resume, picks that
# model without the compiled neutral value (the control) and the lead's own
# model with it ("" in the flag-settings env).
#
# The fence's cold start (protocol-3 shim plus a launcher answering premodel,
# 300 runs each, bytecode warm, 16 CPUs): CPython 3.14.6 p99 0.13 / 0.26 /
# 0.43 / 2.57 s at 0, 16, 32 and 64 CPU burners (max 3.33 s); CPython 3.15.0
# p99 0.17 / 0.45 / 1.75 / 3.47 s (max 4.31 s). Its budget is 15 s.
#
# The fence and security checks, same client and receipts, 2026-10-24. A
# managed-settings file is mounted at /etc/claude-code inside the namespace
# (tests/_client_policy.py: /etc rebuilt entry by entry over a tmpfs with
# bwrap options bubblewrap 0.9 has); the client ignores
# CLAUDE_CODE_MANAGED_SETTINGS_PATH.
#
# The fork gate (tests/test_client_agents.py ForkGateTests):
client check fork-gate: PASS class=FG-off
# Against CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1 and an Agent(fork) allow in the user,
# project and local settings and the variable in the process environment:
# with the compiled deny alone the gate is on and every fork is refused
# naming the rule; with the compiled CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 no fork is
# offered (headless fresh and --resume, lead and cm agent; terminal), and a
# terminal session offers run_in_background again (forced into the
# background with the gate on). Client 2.1.292 (the 2.0.1 pin): with the
# 2.0.1 permissions a terminal lead fork starts (the gap); the variable alone
# closes it. Its revert: without the compiled variable every run is
# "denied" (FG-gate-on).
#
# An agent.spawn mod (tests/test_client_spawn_mod.py):
client check spawn-mod: PASS class=SM-fenced
# Fence membership. A mod rewriting every spawn to a model outside the
# fence: fresh, resumed and workflow agents land on the lead's model, never
# the rewritten one. A rewrite of a resumed agent only: ignored ("a hook can
# only refuse a resumed agent's run"). A managed allowManagedHooksOnly: the
# mod is not loaded (no rewrite logged).
client check spawn-mod-binding: FAIL class=SB-rebound
# The compiled binding, a known failure (expectedFailure; no gate): the
# outside mod moves every agent to the lead's model, an unmanaged mod
# rewriting to another lineup model moves fresh and workflow agents onto it
# (a resumed agent keeps its spawn's model). A deny Agent(model:*) refuses
# the rewritten Agent-tool spawn but not the workflow agent's; it would also
# refuse the lead's own per-call model override, and a Workflow script's own
# model option moves a workflow agent with or without it. The compiled
# --settings scope keeps hooks enabled for charmer's own hooks, so only
# managed settings (allowManagedHooksOnly, which stops those hooks too) keep
# mods out. Whether to compile the partial deny, or to state the weaker
# fence-membership guarantee, is open.
#
# MCP rules and policy (tests/test_client_mcp_policy.py):
client check mcp-policy: PASS class=MCP-named-deny-first
# Servers fx, fx_ and fx__x: allow mcp__<server>__* grants each; allow
# mcp__fx__* or mcp__fx grants fx alone; deny mcp__fx__x removes that whole
# server (fx still runs). The bare allows mcp__fx_ and mcp__fx__x grant
# nothing (observed while building the check): whole-server access is
# mcp__<server>__*. A managed deniedMcpServers keeps a user server from
# starting at launch, on --resume and at a terminal session's start, an
# agent's own server from starting at its spawn, and a plugin server added
# after the terminal start (plugin:mcpfix:fxreload) from starting on
# /reload-plugins (each starts without the policy, the reload's only after
# the command). A plugin server's policy name is plugin:<plugin>:<server>: a
# managed deny of the bare server name does not cover it (observed while
# building the check). A user-settings deniedMcpServers did the same at
# launch.
#
# Token destinations (tests/test_client_gateway_auth.py TokenDestinationPolicyTests):
client check token-destinations: PASS
# ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL only in the managed settings env: the helper token
# reaches the gateway through it and no tripwire host. A helper refresh after
# a 401 (the first token refused): both tokens only on the gateway, in a
# terminal and headless.
#
# Client-side model changes (tests/test_client_fence_substitution.py):
client check fence-substitution: PASS class=FS-fenced
# A refused context-1m beta is resent once without it on the same model; an
# unknown gateway name past 200K tokens compacts and answers on the same
# model; responses naming another model change nothing (one request per
# turn, never that model); a terminal /model to a smaller lead-set model
# fires both switch hooks and stays on the two models (it compacted on the
# new model; no previous-model summary offline); a 404 for claude-fable-5-1
# (by id and by best) is retried on the same model and reported, never moved
# to claude-fable-5 behind the gateway, even with it inside the fence.
#
# The gateway-facing resends and fallbacks of Claude Code 2.1.304-2.1.310
# (tests/test_client_gateway_fallbacks.py), same client and receipts:
client check gateway-fallbacks: PASS class=GF-no-fallback
# Behind a custom base URL every managed request carries the effort beta with
# output_config.effort, context_management with its beta, tool search
# (ToolSearch and DeferredToolPlaceholder; SendMessage, WebFetch, WebSearch,
# the cron, worktree and MCP tools listed by name and fetched as

# fixture gateway refusing effort or context_management gets one resend
# without it; refusing tool search, two (the last without ToolSearch).
client check gateway-fallbacks-gateway: PASS class=GFG-accepted-once
# The 8.0.33 gateway's Claude account route (fresh, resumed with a ToolSearch
# round trip, a terminal /model to claude-fable-5-1): every request answered
# 200 once; the upstream keeps output_config.effort and its beta,

client check mcp-http-retry: PASS class=MR-changing-once
# An HTTP MCP call held while three reset server-message streams make the
# client close the connection: a read-only tool is called again (2 calls), a
# changing tool once (an error result). The previous pin 2.1.302 calls both
# again. A reset or a truncated answer to the call itself is a tool error

client check keepalive: PASS class=KA-one-request
# 50 s of keep-alive pings after message_start, then the content: one
# request, success, under CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1.
# The signed-history matrix (tests/test_client_hooks.py): a refused (400)
# signed-thinking request whose error the client does not recognise is sent
# four times (twice as sent, then twice without tool search) before the 400
# shows, each carrying the block byte-exact; 2.1.302 sent it once.
